neighbours.label: the tokens just after a stated capability or enablement ("can … this way,", "allowing for a", "we could all"): the continuation once an ability has been expressed; the + pole is the copula/verb before "able"
fire: With a library card, students can borrow laptops this way, free of charge.
The hinges are removable, allowing for a quick change of doors.
Any phone with a camera can scan and pay for parking this way, direct from the kerb.
The software is open source, allowing for a great variety of custom plugins.
Once the ice melts, you can reach the island at any time, and return the same day.
The telescope is fully automated, so observers can track a comet remotely, save the images and share them.
The trays stack neatly, allowing for a compact kitchen and easier storage.
Using the portal, tenants can report faults online, follow the repair and rate the service.
quiet: With a library card in her pocket, the student carried the laptops home, free of charge.
The hinges were rusty, and a quick change of doors cost us the whole weekend.
A man with a camera stood by the parking meter, direct from the airport, looking lost.
The software was written in 1998 and shipped with a great variety of custom plugins.
After the ice melted, the island was green for a time, and the birds came back the same day.
The telescope was sold in March, and the observers packed the images and left them.
The trays were stacked neatly in a compact kitchen beside the storage room.
Near the portal, tenants gathered in the cold, grumbled about the repair and went home.

notes: Card: peaks ',' ' a' ' could' ' you' in can/could/allowing-for contexts; output direction reversed suppresses ' able'/' can'. Probes: 0.83 / 0.61 / 0.30 / 0.30 on ability sentences, 0.25 / 0.18 / 0.01 on the same events told as plain past. Fairly broad pole (0.7% of tokens reach 0.1 of max), so near misses may fire weakly.
